title: fix(metadata-protocol): batchData's by-id upsert chooses its arm by what the caller can read
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` teaches how the batch `upsert` chooses between update and create (a `git grep -i upsert` of `skills/` names the import and seed upserts and the generated-route table only), so no skill line changes.

## 维护者速读
- 改了什么：`POST /data/:object/batch` 的 `upsert`(protocol 的 `batchData`)里带 `id` 的行，改为按调用方能读到什么来选「更新」还是「新建」。调用方读得到的记录照旧走更新，仍由引擎判写权限；读不到的 id 按新建处理，答复与同 id 的 create 完全一致。只改 `protocol-batch-data.ts` 这一处分叉。
- 为什么改：QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)
- 风险与回滚：只换答复、不改接受集。调用方读不到的那一行，现在收到同 id 的 create 会收到的答复；读得到的行、无 id 的行、原子批的回滚、无上下文的进程内调用都不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR,不涉及数据迁移。
- 先看：`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts` 的 `case 'upsert'` 分叉(风险 hunk:`objectReadable` 与调用方 `findOne` 两行)和新函数 `callerMayReadObject`;其次 `protocol.upsert-existence.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1 test/upsert-by-id-caller-read.dogfood.test.ts`,预期 28/28 通过(单租户 showcase 19 个，两组织隔离启动 9 个)。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`batchData`'s by-id `upsert` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts`, the `case 'upsert'` fork of `runBatchDataLoop`) now chooses its arm by what the **caller** can read, under the context the arm's write runs with:

1. the object-level read admission, asked once per loop of the `security` service's `canReadObject` (the engine middleware's own read gate, `callerMayReadObject`); a context-less call, or a host whose security service lacks the method, is not asked, and the row read below still enforces there;
2. the caller's own `findOne` by id, where RLS, sharing and the organization wall apply. Inside the atomic arm that context carries the transaction.

A row the caller can read keeps the update arm, where `engine.update` still judges the write. Any other id takes the create arm, the same `engine.insert` call and row builder that `case 'create'` uses, so the row answers exactly as a create naming that id answers on the same door. No new code, field, detail or sentence; nothing names another organization. There is still no fallback insert after an update failure.

The fork's code comment records why this reverses the earlier existence fork, citing ruling 5985885287 (#21771) and the 2026-11-01 maintainer ruling that extends ruling 5934879010 (#21185, rule 2). `BatchDataHost` trades `probeRecord` (no batch body reads it any more) for `getServicesRegistry`; the OCC path and `probeRecord`'s own readers are untouched. The read's options are typed (`EngineQueryOptionsParsed`), not erased.

## Tests

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.upsert-existence.test.ts`, rewritten (11 cases): an unreadable row takes the insert arm and its row refusal deep-equals a batch create's for the same id, store untouched; the fork reads with the caller's context, never the system's; an object the security service refuses sends every row to the insert arm without a row read, asked once per loop; an admitted object still forks on the row read; a throwing admission fails the row and writes nothing; a context-less call is not asked; no fallback insert after an update failure; missing id inserts; readable row updates with the caller's context; atomic rollback with the causal row's create refusal and both reads on the transaction; mixed batch.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/upsert-by-id-caller-read.dogfood.test.ts`, new (28 cases), at the HTTP door, atomic and non-atomic. Stock showcase: create without edit on a private row, create and edit on a private row, a create-only principal with no read; each answers the batch create's body for the same id (row `id` echo aside), with the plain create's `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` code and status, row byte-identical, and an unknown id is created. A readable row with edit is updated; a readable row without edit keeps the update arm's refusal; a refused-both control answers one refusal for an existing and an unknown id. Walled boot (`multiTenant: true`, `isolated`, invitation-only, two organizations created over `/auth/organization/create`): an editor and a creator in organization B on organization A's row get the create's answer, which names neither organization A's id, name nor slug; the editor updates its own organization's row and the creator gets the update arm's refusal.
- `protocol.readonly-insert.test.ts`: one comment names the fork's read.

## Acceptance notes

- Clause-② `no`: the accept set does not move. A row the caller can read takes the same arm as before. A row it cannot read never reaches the update arm: it takes the create arm and answers as a create naming that id. Only the refusal that row receives changes, to the create's (the precedent is the order change that landed as `no` in #28615). No `(narrowing)` arm was found.
- On `driver-memory`, which declares primary-key uniqueness out of its scope, a create naming an existing id lands a second row; the upsert's create arm now does what the create does there. The fork's comment states it. No store enforcing the key (SQL, sqlite-wasm, Turso) is affected.
